Computation time

Source: vignettes/articles/simFastBOIN-speed.Rmd
simFastBOIN-speed.Rmd

The simulation engines of the package are written in C++. This article gives the time that each design takes to simulate the trials of one scenario and to summarize their operating characteristics, on one machine. The times are read from inst/benchmark/results/benchmark.csv, written by inst/benchmark/benchmark.R.

What is measured

The 10 designs that have a reference implementation in another R package are run by both with the same settings and the same number of trials: those of the comparison of the design in inst/validation/, or of the README for the BOIN design, with the number of trials used there for the reference package. The 11 designs without a reference implementation are run by the package alone, with the settings of the example in their vignette and 10,000 trials. The settings are listed in the section “Settings” below.

The time is the elapsed time of one call. A fast call is repeated until the repetitions take at least one second, and the time per call is kept. Every time was measured 3 times, alternating between the two implementations, and the tables give the median. Printed output and warnings of the calls are discarded. The package was installed before it was timed: devtools::load_all() compiles the C++ code without optimization.

The machine

The times were measured on 2026-11-26 under Windows 11 x64 (build 26200), on an Intel(R) Core(TM) Ultra 7 155H with 16 physical cores, with R 4.6.1. The simulations of the package run on one core. The versions of the packages were

Package Version
simFastBOIN 2.2.0.9000
BOIN 2.7.2
boinet 1.6.0
bfboinet 1.1.0
UnifiedDoseFinding 0.1.10
escalation 0.2.3

Designs with a reference implementation

Design Trials Reference Reference (s) simFastBOIN simFastBOIN (s) Times faster
BOIN 10,000 BOIN::get.oc() 12 sim_boin() 0.044 260
BOIN combination 1,000 BOIN::get.oc.comb() 0.8 sim_comb_boin() 0.13 5.9
Waterfall 500 BOIN::get.oc.comb(mtd.contour = TRUE) 2 sim_waterfall() 0.08 25
BOIN-ET 5,000 boinet::boinet() 25 sim_boin_et() 0.044 560
TITE-BOIN-ET 2,000 boinet::tite.boinet() 58 sim_tite_boin_et() 0.061 960
gBOIN-ET 5,000 boinet::gboinet() 25 sim_gboin_et() 0.14 170
TITE-gBOIN-ET 5,000 boinet::tite.gboinet() 150 sim_tite_gboin_et() 0.4 390
BF-BOIN-ET 1,000 bfboinet::get.oc.backboinet() 340 sim_bf_boin_et() 0.032 11,000
gBOIN 4,000 UnifiedDoseFinding::get_oc_QuasiBOIN() 6.8 sim_gboin() 0.021 320
BOIN12 2,000 escalation::simulate_trials() 140 sim_boin12() 0.042 3,300

The package was between 5.9 and 11,000 times faster than the reference implementation. The ratio is smallest for the two drug-combination designs, 5.9 for the BOIN drug-combination design and 25 for the waterfall design: both packages select the MTD of every trial with the bivariate isotonic regression of Iso::biviso(), called from R once per trial. It is largest for BF-BOIN-ET, whose reference implementation takes 340 seconds for 1,000 trials.

Designs without a reference implementation

Design Trials simFastBOIN Seconds
iBOIN 10,000 sim_iboin() 0.053
Accelerated BOIN 10,000 sim_boin() 0.039
TITE-BOIN, imputation 10,000 sim_tite_boin() 0.074
TITE-BOIN, ESS 10,000 sim_tite_boin() 0.093
BF-BOIN 10,000 sim_bf_boin() 0.16
BE-BOIN 10,000 sim_be_boin() 0.17
TITE-BOIN12 10,000 sim_tite_boin12() 0.84
U-BOIN 10,000 sim_uboin() 0.19
Comb-BOIN12 10,000 sim_comb_boin12() 96
TITE-Comb-BOIN12 10,000 sim_tite_comb_boin12() 94
BOIN-ETC 10,000 sim_boin_etc() 0.12

9 of the 11 designs take less than one second for 10,000 trials. Comb-BOIN12 and TITE-Comb-BOIN12 take about 96 and 94 seconds: by default (est_method = "logistic") they estimate the response probabilities at the end of every trial by the posterior mean under the logistic model of Lu et al. (2025), computed by importance sampling with 4,000 points (n_draws = 4000). With est_method = "observed", the observed response rates, the selection is much faster.

The scripts named in the settings are in inst/validation/, and the scenarios of the articles are taken from the scripts of inst/reproduce/.

Measuring on your own machine

From the root of the source package, install the package, restart R and run

library(simFastBOIN)
source("inst/benchmark/benchmark.R")
res <- run_benchmark()

with the reference packages ‘BOIN’, ‘boinet’, ‘bfboinet’, ‘UnifiedDoseFinding’ and ‘escalation’ installed; a design whose package is missing is recorded as such. The run writes inst/benchmark/results/benchmark.csv. Most of the time goes to the reference packages.

References

Lu, M., Zhang, J., Yuan, Y. and Lin, R. (2025). Comb-BOIN12: A utility-based Bayesian optimal interval design for dose optimization in cancer drug-combination trials. Statistics in Biopharmaceutical Research, 17(2), 266-276.
